(B) the person should not give, or continue to give, evidence relating to a particular matter before the Committee; or
the person should not produce documents to the Committee; or
the person should not produce documents of a particular kind to the Committee;
the Minister may give to the presiding member of the Committee a certificate in relation to the matter stating the Minister’s opinion.
The Minister’s certificate must also specify:

in a case to which subparagraph (1)(b)(ii) or (v) applies—the matter in relation to which the Minister is satisfied that the person should not give, or continue to give, evidence, or specifying the kind of documents that the Minister is satisfied the person should not produce, as the case requires; and
in a case to which sub-subparagraph (1)(b)(iii)(B) applies—the matter in relation to which the Minister is satisfied that the person should not give, or continue to give, evidence.

The Minister must give a copy of a certificate under subclause (1) to the President of the Senate, to the Speaker of the House of Representatives and to the person required to give evidence or produce documents.
A decision of the Minister under subclause (1) must not be questioned in any court or tribunal.
Where the Minister gives a certificate under subclause (1) in relation to a person:

if the certificate states that the person should not give, or continue to give, evidence before the Committee—the Committee must not receive, or continue to receive, as the case may be, evidence from the person; or

if the certificate states that the person should not give, or continue to give, evidence before the Committee relating to a particular matter—the Committee must not receive, or continue to receive, as the case may be, evidence from the person relating to that matter; or

if the certificate states that the person should not produce documents, or documents of a particular kind, to the Committee—the Committee must not receive documents, or documents of that kind, as the case may be, from the person.
The Committee may take evidence on oath or affirmation.
The member presiding may administer an oath or affirmation to a witness appearing before the Committee.
The oath or affirmation is an oath or affirmation that the evidence the person will give will be true.
(4) To avoid doubt, the Committee is not to be taken to be an Australian court for the purposes of the Evidence Act 1995.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Publication of evidence or contents of documents

content.p: Subject to this clause, the Committee may disclose or publish, or authorise the disclosure or publication of:
any evidence taken by the Committee; or
the contents of any document produced to the Committee.

If the evidence is taken, or the document is produced, in a review conducted in private, the Committee must not disclose or publish, or authorise the disclosure or publication of the evidence or the contents of the document without the written authority of:
if the person who gave the evidence or produced the document is a staff member of an agency—the agency head; or
in any other case—the person who gave the evidence or produced the document.
Subclause (2) does not apply:
if the evidence, or the contents of the document, have already been lawfully disclosed or published; or
in relation to a matter of which the Committee has become aware otherwise than because of the giving of any evidence before, or the production of any document to, the Committee.

The Committee must not disclose or publish, or authorise the disclosure or publication of, the evidence, or the contents of the document, if the disclosure or publication would disclose a matter that the Committee is not, under clause 7, permitted to disclose in a report to a House of the Parliament.

The Committee must obtain the advice of the responsible Minister or responsible Ministers concerned if the Committee considers that it is reasonably likely that the disclosure or publication might disclose a matter of that kind.
(6) This clause has effect despite section 2 of the Parliamentary Papers Act 1908.

(7) If the evidence, or the contents of the document, are disclosed or published under this clause, section 4 of the Parliamentary Papers Act 1908 applies to the disclosure or publication as if it were a publication under an authority given under section 2 of that Act.
Certain information not to be disclosed
The Committee must not disclose in a report to a House of the Parliament:
the identity of a person who is or has been a staff member of ASIO or ASIS or an agent of ACIC, ASIO, ASIS, AGO or ASD; or
any information from which the identity of such a person could reasonably be inferred; or
operationally sensitive information or information that would or might prejudice:
Australia’s national security or the conduct of Australia’s foreign relations; or
the performance by an agency of its functions; or
any information the disclosure of which could reveal, or enable a person to ascertain, the existence or identity of a confidential source of information to any agency; or
any information the disclosure of which could endanger a person’s life or physical safety; or
any information the disclosure of which could prejudice the protection of public safety; or
any information the disclosure of which could prejudice the fair trial of a person or the impartial adjudication of a matter; or
any information the disclosure of which could prejudice the proper enforcement of the law or the operations of law enforcement authorities; or
any information the disclosure of which could unreasonably disclose confidential commercial information; or
any information:
having a national security classification; or
that the Committee believes should have a national security classification;
unless the agency head of the agency that produced the information, or from which the information originated, provides written authority to disclose the information.
An agency head may determine that paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) do not apply to the identification of specified staff members or agents of his or her agency, and the determination has effect accordingly.

The Committee must obtain the advice of the responsible Minister or responsible Ministers concerned as to whether the disclosure of any part of the report would or might disclose a matter referred to in subclause (1).

The Committee must not present a report of the Committee to a House of the Parliament if a responsible Minister concerned has advised that the report or a part of the report would or might disclose such a matter.
If:
any evidence or document about a matter has been taken by or produced to the Committee as constituted at a time; and
either of the following happens before the Committee reports on the matter:
the Committee as so constituted ceases to exist;
the constitution of the Committee changes;
the Committee as constituted at a later time, whether during the same or another Parliament, may consider the evidence or document as if the evidence or document had been taken by or produced to it.
Clause 9 applies to each member of the later Committee as if the evidence or document had been taken or produced to that Committee.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Offences relating to publishing or disclosing evidence or documents

content.p: A person (including a member) commits an offence if:
the person discloses or publishes any evidence taken by, or the contents of any document produced to, the Committee in a review conducted in private; and
the disclosure or publication is not authorised in writing by:
if the person who gave the evidence or produced the document is a staff member of an agency—the agency head; or
in any other case—the person who gave the evidence or produced the document; and
the disclosure or publication is of evidence, or is of the contents of a document, that has not already been lawfully disclosed or published.

Subclause (1) does not apply to the disclosure or publication by a person of a matter of which the person has become aware otherwise than because of the giving of any evidence before, or the production of any document to, the Committee.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
(3) Subclause (1) has effect despite section 2 of the Parliamentary Papers Act 1908.
In this clause:
Committee includes the Parliamentary Joint Committee on the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation.

Note: The Parliamentary Joint Committee on the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (established under the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979) ceased to exist when the Parliamentary Joint Committee on ASIO, ASIS and DSD was established. However, the records of the earlier Committee were transferred to the Parliamentary Joint Committee on ASIO, ASIS and DSD.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Offences relating to giving evidence or producing documents

content.p: A person who has been given a notice requiring the person to appear before the Committee commits an offence if the person:
fails to attend as required by the notice; or
having not been excused or released by the Committee, fails to attend and report from day to day; or
refuses or fails to be sworn or to make an affirmation; or
refuses or fails to answer a question, not being a question about a matter in respect of which a certificate has been issued under clause 4, that the Committee requires the person to answer.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 6 months or 30 penalty units, or both.
Subclause (1) applies to a staff member who is nominated by an agency head under subclause 3(5) to appear before the Committee to give evidence.
Paragraph (1)(d) does not apply if the answer to the question would tend to incriminate the person.

A person who has been given a notice requiring the person to produce a document, not being a document in respect of which a certificate has been issued under clause 4, to the Committee commits an offence if the person refuses or fails to produce the document.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 6 months or 30 penalty units, or both.
Subclause (4) does not apply if the producing of the document would tend to incriminate the person.
A person commits an offence if the person:
gives evidence to the Committee; and
does so knowing that the evidence is false or misleading in a material particular.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
A person who causes or threatens to cause any detriment to another person with the intention that the other person or a third person will:
not attend as a witness before the Committee; or
give false evidence or a falsified document to the Committee; or
withhold true evidence or a document from the Committee;
commits an offence.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
A person who otherwise improperly influences another person with the intention that the other person or a third person will:
not attend as a witness before the Committee; or
give false evidence or a falsified document to the Committee; or
withhold true evidence or a document from the Committee;
commits an offence.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.

A person who causes or threatens to cause any detriment to another person because that other person or a third person appeared before the Committee or produced a document to the Committee commits an offence.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 5 years or 300 penalty units, or both.
A person who is or has been a member, or a member of the staff, of the Committee commits an offence if the person, directly or indirectly:
makes a record of, or discloses or communicates to a person, any information acquired because of holding the office or employment; or
produces to a person a document provided to the Committee for the purposes of enabling the Committee to perform its functions;
and the action of the person is not carried out for the purposes of enabling the Committee to perform its functions.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
A person who is or has been a member, or a member of the staff, of the Committee must not be required to:
produce in a court a document of which he or she has custody, or to which he or she has access, because of his or her position as a member, or a member of the staff, of the Committee; or
disclose or to communicate to a court any information obtained by him or her because of such a position.
In this clause:
produce includes permit access to.
A prosecution for an offence against this Part can be instituted only by the Attorney-General or with the Attorney-General’s consent.
The members who are members of the House of Representatives must be appointed by resolution of the House on the nomination of the Prime Minister.
Before nominating the members, the Prime Minister must consult with the Leader of each recognised political party that is represented in the House and does not form part of the Government.
The members who are Senators must be appointed by resolution of the Senate on the nomination of the Leader of the Government in the Senate.

Before nominating the members, the Leader of the Government in the Senate must consult with the Leader of each recognised political party that is represented in the Senate and does not form part of the Government.

In nominating the members, the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Government in the Senate must have regard to the desirability of ensuring that the composition of the Committee reflects the representation of recognised political parties in the Parliament.
A person is not eligible for appointment as a member if the person is:
a Minister; or
the President of the Senate; or
the Speaker of the House of Representatives.
A member holds office during the pleasure of the House of the Parliament by which the member was appointed.
A member ceases to hold office as a member:
when the House of Representatives expires by the passing of time or is dissolved; or
if the person becomes the holder of an office specified in any of the paragraphs of subclause 14(6); or
if the person ceases to be a member of the House of the Parliament by which the person was appointed; or
if the person resigns the office.
A member who is a Senator may resign his or her office by giving a signed notice of resignation to the President of the Senate.
A member who is a member of the House of Representatives may resign his or her office by giving a signed notice of resignation to the Speaker of the House of Representatives.
Either House of the Parliament may appoint one of its members to fill a vacancy among the members of the Committee appointed by that House.
There must be a Chair of the Committee who must be a Government member elected by the members from time to time.
The Chair holds office during the pleasure of the Committee.
A person holding office as Chair ceases to hold the office if:
the person ceases to be a member; or
the person resigns the office.
A person holding office as Chair may resign the office by giving a signed notice of resignation to a meeting of the Committee.
There must be a Deputy Chair of the Committee who must be a member elected by the members from time to time.
The Deputy Chair holds office during the pleasure of the Committee.
A person holding office as Deputy Chair ceases to hold the office if:
the person ceases to be a member; or
the person resigns the office.
A person holding office as Deputy Chair may resign the office by giving a signed notice of resignation to a meeting of the Committee.
The Committee may, subject to subclause (3), meet physically or using virtual meeting technology:
as the Committee decides by resolution; or
subject to a resolution of the Committee, as the Chair decides.
The Committee may meet and transact business even though the Parliament has been prorogued.

If classified information may be discussed at meetings, the Chair must obtain and follow the advice of the agency head of each agency that produces such information, or from which such information originates, regarding the suitability of the security arrangements for such meetings (including the security arrangements for virtual meeting technology).
The Chair must preside at all meetings of the Committee at which he or she is present.
If:
the Chair is not present at a meeting of the Committee; and
either:
the meeting is one at which a question is to be decided by voting, or could reasonably be expected to be so decided; or

throughout a continuous period of more than one month immediately preceding the day of the meeting, the Chair was absent from duty or from Australia, or was for any reason unable to perform the duties of his or her office as Chair;
the members present are to appoint a Government member to preside.
If:
the Chair is not present at a meeting of the Committee; and
the members are not required by subclause (5) to appoint a Government member to preside;
then:
if the Deputy Chair is present at the meeting—the Deputy Chair is to preside; or
if the Deputy Chair is not present at the meeting—the members present are to appoint a member to preside.
A member who presides at a meeting of the Committee under subclause (5) or (5A) may exercise, in relation to the meeting and any matter arising out of the meeting, any of the powers of the Chair.
The Committee must keep minutes of its proceedings.
At a meeting of the Committee, a quorum is constituted if:
at least 7 members are present; and
subject to subclause (2), a majority of the members present are Government members.
There may be an equal number of Government members and non-Government members if the presiding member is a Government member.
A question arising at a meeting is to be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting.
The member presiding at the meeting has a deliberative vote.
The member presiding at the meeting has a casting vote if votes are equal.
The proceedings of the Committee are to be conducted in the manner determined by the Committee.
The Committee must not conduct a review in public without the approval of:
the Minister responsible for ASIO; and
the Minister responsible for ASIS; and
the Minister responsible for AGO, DIO and ASD; and
the Minister responsible for ONI.

The Committee may give directions as to the persons who may be present at a meeting conducted in private. In giving such directions, the Committee must have regard to the requirements of security and any other matters the Committee thinks fit.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Staff of the Committee must be cleared for security purposes

content.p: Each member of the staff of the Committee must be cleared for security purposes at least at a level and frequency:
appropriate for access to information and systems at the classification that the staff member requires, in accordance with government policy in relation to protective security; and
acceptable to all of the agency heads.
The Committee must make arrangements acceptable to all of the agency heads for the security of any information held and any records made by the Committee.

The Committee must ensure that any document with a national security classification provided to the Committee is returned or destroyed as soon as possible after the members have examined it in accordance with an arrangement acceptable to the agency that produced the document.
Establishment
The Committee may appoint one or more subcommittees to inquire into and report to the Committee in relation to matters concerning the Committee as the Committee directs.
Membership
A subcommittee must consist of at least 3 of the Committee’s members.
The Chair and Deputy Chair of the Committee are ex officio members of each subcommittee.
Reporting
A subcommittee must report in writing to the Committee as soon as practicable on each matter referred to that subcommittee by the Committee.
Sitting times
A subcommittee may sit at any time, including at a time when the Committee is sitting.
A member of a subcommittee holds office during the pleasure of the Committee.
A member of a subcommittee ceases to hold office if:
the person ceases to be a member of the Committee; or
the person resigns the office.
A member of a subcommittee may resign his or her office by giving a signed notice of resignation to the Chair of the Committee.
(1AA) The Committee may elect a Chair and Deputy Chair for each subcommittee.
A subcommittee may determine matters relating to the operation of the subcommittee, except as mentioned in subsection (2).
If the Chair of the Committee gives a direction to a subcommittee in relation to the operation of the subcommittee, the subcommittee must operate in accordance with the direction.
At a meeting of a subcommittee, 3 members of that subcommittee, including at least one Government member and one non-Government member, constitute a quorum.
Any member of the Committee may participate in the proceedings of a subcommittee. However, only members of that subcommittee may vote or move a motion.

hcontainer.name: schedule
hcontainer.heading: Activities excepted under subsection 6(5) of the Act

content.p: Note: See section 6.
The provision of a weapon, or training in the use of a weapon or in self-defence techniques, is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if it is provided:
to a person who is a staff member or agent of ASIS; and
for the purpose of enabling the person:
to protect himself or herself; or
to protect a staff member or agent of ASIS; or
to protect a person who is cooperating with ASIS in accordance with section 13; or
to protect another person, or class of persons, specified in the Minister’s approval under subclause (3); or
to provide training to staff members or agents of ASIS; and
in accordance with a Ministerial approval given under subclause (3).
The provision to a person of a weapon, or training in the use of a weapon or in self-defence techniques, is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if:
the person:
is an officer of an authority with which ASIS is cooperating in accordance with paragraph 13(1)(c); or
is an officer (however described) of a Commonwealth authority, or a State authority, and is authorised in that capacity to carry and use weapons; and
it is provided in accordance with a Ministerial approval under subclause (3A) in relation to the person; and
it is provided for the purpose of enabling the person:
to protect himself or herself; or
to protect a staff member or agent of ASIS; or
to protect a person who is cooperating with ASIS in accordance with section 13; or
to protect another person, or class of persons, specified in the Minister’s approval under subclause (3A).
The use of a weapon or self-defence techniques is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if:
the weapon or techniques are used:
for a purpose covered by paragraph (1)(b); or
in training in accordance with subclause (1) or (1A); and
in a case covered by any of subparagraphs (1)(b)(i) to (iiia)—the weapon or techniques are used outside Australia; and
guidelines have been issued by the Director-General of ASIS under subclause (6); and
the weapon or techniques are used in compliance with those guidelines.
The use of a weapon or self-defence techniques is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if:
the weapon or techniques are used in the proper performance of a function of ASIS; and
the weapon or techniques are used in a controlled environment; and
guidelines have been issued by the Director-General of ASIS under subclause (6); and
the weapon or techniques are used in compliance with those guidelines.
Example: The following may constitute the use of a weapon or technique in a controlled environment:
the use of a firearm at a rifle range;
the use of a martial art at a martial arts club.
The Minister may, by written notice given to the Director-General of ASIS, approve the provision of a weapon, or training in the use of a weapon or in self-defence techniques, to:
a specified staff member or agent of ASIS; or
the holder of a specified position in ASIS.

The Minister may, by written notice given to the Director-General of ASIS, approve the provision of a weapon, or training in the use of a weapon or in self-defence techniques, to a specified person for the purposes of paragraph (1A)(b).
An approval under subclause (3) or (3A) for the provision of a weapon or training must specify:
the purpose for which the weapon or training is provided; and
any conditions that must be complied with in relation to the provision of the weapon or training; and
if the approval is for the provision of a weapon or training in the use of a weapon—the kind or class of weapon involved.
An approval under subclause (3) for the provision of a weapon or training may specify a person, or class of persons, that may be protected under subparagraph (1)(b)(iiia).
An approval under subclause (3A) for the provision of a weapon or training may specify a person, or class of persons, that may be protected under subparagraph (1A)(c)(iv).

As soon as practicable after giving the Director-General of ASIS an approval under subclause (3) or (3A), the Minister must give the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a copy of the approval.
The Director-General of ASIS must issue guidelines for the purposes of this Schedule on matters related to the use of weapons and self-defence techniques.
As soon as practicable after making or changing the guidelines, the Director-General of ASIS must give the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a copy of the guidelines.
The Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security must brief the Committee on the content and effect of the guidelines if:
the Committee requests the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security to do so; or
the guidelines change.
Guidelines issued under subclause (6) are not legislative instruments.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Application of certain State and Territory laws

content.p: A person is not required under, or by reason of, a law of a State or Territory:
to obtain or have a licence or permission for doing any act or thing in accordance with clause 1; or
to register any weapon provided in accordance with clause 1.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Reports to Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security

content.p: The Director-General of ASIS must give a report to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security if a weapon or self-defence technique is used by a staff member or agent of ASIS against a person for a purpose mentioned in any of subparagraphs 1(1)(b)(i) to (iiia).
The report must:
be given in writing as soon as practicable after the weapon or self-defence technique is used; and
explain the circumstances in which the use of the weapon or self-defence technique occurred.

hcontainer.name: schedule
hcontainer.heading: Activities excepted under subsection 6(5A) of the Act

content.p: Note: See section 6.

The provision of a weapon, or training in the use of force (including in the use of a weapon), for the purposes of activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if it is provided:
to a person who is a staff member or agent of ASIS; and
for the purpose of preventing, mitigating or removing:
a significant risk to a person’s safety; or
(ii) a significant threat to security (within the meaning of paragraphs (a) and (aa) of the definition of security in section 4 of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979); or
a significant risk to the operational security of ASIS from interference by a foreign person or entity; and
in accordance with a Ministerial approval given under paragraph (3)(a).

The use of force (including the use of a weapon) against a person, or the threat of the use of force (including the use of a weapon) against a person, in the course of activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia is not prevented by subsection 6(4) if:
the conduct is by a staff member or agent of ASIS; and
the conduct is for the purpose of preventing, mitigating or removing:
a significant risk to a person’s safety; or
(ii) a significant threat to security (within the meaning of paragraphs (a) and (aa) of the definition of security in section 4 of the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979); or
a significant risk to the operational security of ASIS from interference by a foreign person or entity; and
the conduct is in accordance with a Ministerial approval given under paragraph (3)(b); and
guidelines have been issued by the Director-General of ASIS under clause 2; and
the conduct is in compliance with those guidelines.
Minister’s approval
The Minister may approve:
the provision of a weapon, or training in the use of force (including in the use of a weapon) to:
a specified staff member or agent of ASIS; or
the holder of a specified position in ASIS;
for the purposes of specified activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia; or
the use of force, or the threat of the use of force, against a specified person, or a specified class of persons, by:
a specified staff member or agent of ASIS; or
the holder of a specified position in ASIS;
in the course of specified activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia.
(4) The Minister (the approving Minister) must not give approval under paragraph (3)(b) unless:
the approving Minister has consulted with:
the Prime Minister; and
the Attorney-General; and
the Defence Minister; and
any other Minister who has responsibility for a matter that is likely to be significantly affected by an act that is to be approved; and
the approving Minister is satisfied that:

there are satisfactory arrangements in place to ensure that, in acting under the approval, nothing will be done beyond what is necessary having regard to the purposes for which the approval is given; and

there are satisfactory arrangements in place to ensure that the nature and consequences of acts done under the approval will be reasonable having regard to the purposes for which the approval is given.
An approval under paragraph (3)(a) or (b) must be given by notice in writing to the Director-General of ASIS.
The approval must specify:
any conditions that must be complied with in relation to the conduct approved; and
if the approval is for the provision of a weapon or training in the use of a weapon—the kind or class of weapon involved.
The approval is not a legislative instrument.
As soon as practicable after giving the Director-General of ASIS an approval under paragraph (3)(a) or (b), the Minister must give a copy of the approval to:
the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security; and
if the approval is given under paragraph (3)(b)—the Prime Minister and each other Minister who was consulted about the approval under paragraph (4)(a).
Annual review of approvals
As soon as practicable after each year ending on 30 June, the Minister must:
consider whether the approvals in force under paragraphs (3)(a) and (b) at the end of the year are appropriate; and
in relation to any approval that is no longer appropriate:
amend the approval so that it is appropriate; or
revoke the approval.

In considering whether an approval in force under paragraph (3)(b) at the end of a year is appropriate, the Minister must take into account whether the Minister is still satisfied of the matters mentioned in paragraph (4)(b).
As soon as practicable after subclause (9) has been complied with:
the Director-General of ASIS must give the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a report in writing outlining the action taken under subclause (9); and

if any part of the report relates to an approval under paragraph (3)(b)—the Minister must give a copy of that part of the report to the Prime Minister and each other Minister who was consulted about the approval under paragraph (4)(a).

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Guidelines for the purposes of this Schedule

content.p: The Director-General of ASIS must issue guidelines for the purposes of this Schedule on matters related to:
the use of force (including the use of weapons) against a person in the course of activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia; and
threats of the use of force (including the use of weapons) against a person in the course of activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia.
As soon as practicable after making or changing the guidelines, the Director-General of ASIS must give the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security a copy of the guidelines.
The Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security must brief the Committee on the content and effect of the guidelines if:
the Committee requests the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security to do so; or
the guidelines change.
Guidelines issued under subclause (1) are not legislative instruments.

hcontainer.heading: Application of certain State and Territory laws

content.p: A person is not required under, or by reason of, a law of a State or Territory:
to obtain or have a licence or permission for doing any act or thing in accordance with clause 1; or
to register any weapon provided in accordance with clause 1.

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Reports to Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security

content.p: The Director-General of ASIS must give a report to the Inspector-General of Intelligence and Security if force, or the threat of force, is used by a staff member or agent of ASIS against a person for a purpose mentioned in paragraph 1(2)(b) in the course of activities undertaken by ASIS outside Australia.
The report must:
be given in writing as soon as practicable after the force or threat of force is used; and
explain the circumstances in which the force or threat of force occurred.
In this clause:
the use of force includes but is not limited to the use of a weapon; and
the threat of the use of force includes but is not limited to a threat that involves a weapon.
